title: Display error in 1.26 with login screen
body:
I reverted back to http-basic-auth in 1.26. Essential information about the authentication with the new login screen is not displayed to me. There is full access after authorization because I can, for example, reactivate Basic Auth via the GUI. Browser: Chrome 118. In Firefox the GUI doesn't even build completely, some JS restarts the build every few seconds. After activating http-basic-auth, the GUI works again as usual in Firefox.
![2023-11-09_09-17](https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/assets/33317545/eef74df0-6edc-4c59-b4ee-0f8b631142c7)
![2023-11-09_09-18](https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/assets/33317545/43729a65-9367-4b0b-82b1-14dd7a4a7037)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: We're aware of the issue but weren't able reproduce it yet. Your screenshot is pretty interesting though, as half of the UI appears to work. This almost looks like some kind of race condition.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I can now add the following observation. After I was able to observe the error pattern on two hosts with syncthing increased from 1.25 to 1.26, I switched back to basic-auth as written and the error disappeared. Now I have switched two more hosts and the error didn't even occur on them in the same browser session with the new login mask, which surprised me. Then I switched the two first migrated hosts back to the new login mask as a cross-check, and lo and behold, the error disappeared, as if Chrome had to get used to it... If I can do anything to help find the cause, let me do so let me know.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
I had the "endless reload loop" here (Firefox 118.0.2) on multiple installations of 1.26. Clearing cookies has solved the problem.

These were the cookies before I did that:

| Name             | Path         | Expires | HttpOnly | Secure |
| ---------------- | ------------ | ------- | -------- | ------ |
| CSRF-Token-XXXXX | /            | Session | false    | false  |
| sessionid-XXXXX  | /            | Session | false    | true   |
| sessionid-XXXXX  | /rest        | Session | false    | true   |
| sessionid-XXXXX  | /rest/svc    | Session | false    | true   |
| sessionid-XXXXX  | /rest/system | Session | false    | true   |

After deleting the cookies and logging in again, only CSRF-Token-XXXXX and the sessionid-XXXXX for path "/" were recreated.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body: Had to revert to Basic Auth as well (Chrome here). Clearing cache and cookies did not help. It logged but the interface was broken. Could only login through an anonymous tab.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
So, my interpretation of all this:

- Previously, we did not set `Path: /` on the cookie. Sometimes it ended up on that path, but we also sometimes polluted the cookie space with `/rest` etc cookies as seen above.
- Currently, we set the cookie on `/` but when *getting* the cookie we sometimes get a random cookie for another path that we didn't set. This is an auth failure so we loop.

We can solve this now by either looking at *all* cookies and verifying that we check the one for `/`, or we can use a new cookie name and the old ones should be irrelevant.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body: There's a separate issue that logging *out* will not work as expected if the browser has also cached basic-auth credentials, but that's less critical imho.
